# Cloudy AI Tool Finder: full tool data
Last reviewed 2026-11-10. Pricing and features change often. Facts are based on public sources checked around Nov 2025–Nov 2026; always verify on the vendor site before buying.

## Coding & software engineering
AI coding assistants, IDEs and CLI agents that help you write, refactor and ship software faster.

### Cursor
- Website: https://cursor.com
- Page: https://itscloudy96.github.io/ai-tool-finder/tool/cursor/
- Pricing: Free (limited); Plus from ~$8/mo (Grok-only); Pro ~$16–30/mo; usage meters apply (tier: freemium, free tier: yes)
- Best for: Complex multi-file projects and daily vibe coding in a dedicated AI IDE
- Skill levels: beginner, intermediate, advanced
- Strengths: AI-native VS Code fork; Strong multi-file agent/Composer; Codebase indexing and MCP
- Weaknesses: Must switch editors; Usage meters can surprise heavy users; Steeper for non-developers

### Claude Code
- Website: https://claude.ai/code
- Page: https://itscloudy96.github.io/ai-tool-finder/tool/claude-code/
- Pricing: Minimal on Free; full access with Claude Pro from $17/mo annual ($20 monthly); Max $100–200/mo (tier: freemium, free tier: yes)
- Best for: Large codebases, terminal agents, and long-horizon debugging
- Skill levels: intermediate, advanced
- Strengths: 1M-token context for large repos; Terminal-first autonomous refactors; Strong planning and git workflows
- Weaknesses: Free tier too limited for real coding; CLI learning curve; Shares Claude chat usage pool

### GitHub Copilot
- Website: https://github.com/features/copilot
- Page: https://itscloudy96.github.io/ai-tool-finder/tool/github-copilot/
- Pricing: Free (2,000 completions + 50 chat/agent requests/mo); Pro $10/mo; Pro+ $39/mo (tier: freemium, free tier: yes)
- Best for: Developers who want AI in VS Code/JetBrains without switching editors
- Skill levels: beginner, intermediate, advanced
- Strengths: Stays in your existing IDE; Best value paid coding AI; Native GitHub PR/issue workflows
- Weaknesses: Less deep codebase context than Cursor/Claude Code; Agent depth more scoped

### OpenAI Codex
- Website: https://chatgpt.com/codex
- Page: https://itscloudy96.github.io/ai-tool-finder/tool/codex/
- Pricing: Included with ChatGPT Plus ($20/mo) and Pro ($200/mo); API usage extra (tier: paid, free tier: no)
- Best for: OpenAI-first teams who want coding inside the ChatGPT stack
- Skill levels: beginner, intermediate, advanced
- Strengths: Runs in ChatGPT, CLI, and IDE extensions; Agentic plan-run-iterate loop; Same login as ChatGPT
- Weaknesses: Tied to OpenAI models; Heavy use may need Pro or API

### Devin Desktop (Windsurf)
- Website: https://windsurf.com
- Page: https://itscloudy96.github.io/ai-tool-finder/tool/devin-desktop/
- Pricing: Free plan; Pro from ~$15–20/mo (tier: freemium, free tier: yes)
- Best for: Budget-conscious AI IDE users and Cognition stack fans
- Skill levels: intermediate, advanced
- Strengths: AI-native IDE with Cascade/Devin Local; Persists project context across sessions; Unlimited Tab on free/paid
- Weaknesses: Brand/naming churn (Windsurf to Devin Desktop); Smaller community than Cursor

### Replit Agent
- Website: https://replit.com
- Page: https://itscloudy96.github.io/ai-tool-finder/tool/replit/
- Pricing: Free Starter with daily Agent credits; Core from ~$17–20/mo annual (tier: freemium, free tier: yes)
- Best for: Beginners and fast browser-hosted prototypes
- Skill levels: beginner, intermediate
- Strengths: Browser IDE, no local setup; Agent asks clarifying questions first; Build and host in one place
- Weaknesses: Less stack control than local IDEs; Agent occasionally over-claims fixes

### v0 by Vercel
- Website: https://v0.dev
- Page: https://itscloudy96.github.io/ai-tool-finder/tool/v0/
- Pricing: Free (~$5 credits/mo + daily message limits); Premium from $20/mo (tier: freemium, free tier: yes)
- Best for: Generating production-looking UI fast, then wiring logic elsewhere
- Skill levels: beginner, intermediate
- Strengths: Polished React/Tailwind UI generation; Shows plan before writing code; Great for landing pages and dashboards
- Weaknesses: Frontend/UI focused, not full-stack; Restrictive free plan

### Bolt.new
- Website: https://bolt.new
- Page: https://itscloudy96.github.io/ai-tool-finder/tool/bolt/
- Pricing: Free includes token allowance; paid plans for more usage (tier: freemium, free tier: yes)
- Best for: Vibe coding full apps and simple browser games from a prompt
- Skill levels: beginner, intermediate
- Strengths: Prompt-to-full-stack apps in browser; Fast iteration for demos; Good for beginners shipping apps/games
- Weaknesses: Token limits on free; Less control for large production apps

### Lovable
- Website: https://lovable.dev
- Page: https://itscloudy96.github.io/ai-tool-finder/tool/lovable/
- Pricing: Free with daily build credits; paid for higher quotas (tier: freemium, free tier: yes)
- Best for: Non-engineers shipping polished web app MVPs quickly
- Skill levels: beginner, intermediate
- Strengths: Chat-to-app builder; Quick MVPs and landing sites; Friendly for non-engineers
- Weaknesses: Credit limits; Not ideal for complex monorepos

### Aider
- Website: https://aider.chat
- Page: https://itscloudy96.github.io/ai-tool-finder/tool/aider/
- Pricing: Free open-source CLI; you pay for the model API you connect (tier: free, free tier: yes)
- Best for: CLI power users who want pay-as-you-go coding agents
- Skill levels: intermediate, advanced
- Strengths: Git-first diffs; Bring your own keys/models; Strong multi-file refactors
- Weaknesses: No polished GUI; Requires API keys and terminal comfort

### Continue
- Website: https://continue.dev
- Page: https://itscloudy96.github.io/ai-tool-finder/tool/continue-dev/
- Pricing: Free open-source; bring your own models/API keys (tier: free, free tier: yes)
- Best for: Privacy-first or local-model coding setups
- Skill levels: intermediate, advanced
- Strengths: Open-source VS Code/JetBrains extension; Local or hosted models; MCP support
- Weaknesses: You manage models and quality; Less turnkey than Cursor

### Amazon Q Developer
- Website: https://aws.amazon.com/q/developer/
- Page: https://itscloudy96.github.io/ai-tool-finder/tool/amazon-q/
- Pricing: Free (50 agentic requests + 1,000 lines/mo); Pro from $19/user/mo (tier: freemium, free tier: yes)
- Best for: Teams deep in the AWS ecosystem
- Skill levels: intermediate, advanced
- Strengths: AWS account + docs context; IDE and CLI; Enterprise compliance options
- Weaknesses: AWS-centric; Free tier capped

### Tabnine
- Website: https://www.tabnine.com
- Page: https://itscloudy96.github.io/ai-tool-finder/tool/tabnine/
- Pricing: Free basic completions; Code Assistant Platform from $39/user/mo annual (tier: freemium, free tier: yes)
- Best for: Regulated enterprises needing private AI coding
- Skill levels: intermediate, advanced
- Strengths: Zero code retention options; VPC/on-prem/air-gapped; Team governance
- Weaknesses: Expensive vs consumer tools; Less agentic than Cursor/Claude Code

### Zed AI
- Website: https://zed.dev
- Page: https://itscloudy96.github.io/ai-tool-finder/tool/zed/
- Pricing: Editor free; AI features tied to Zed account/plans (tier: freemium, free tier: yes)
- Best for: Developers who want a fast native editor with AI assist
- Skill levels: intermediate, advanced
- Strengths: Fast native editor; Collaborative editing; Growing AI assistance
- Weaknesses: Smaller AI ecosystem than Cursor; Fewer agent tutorials

### ChatGPT
- Website: https://chatgpt.com
- Page: https://itscloudy96.github.io/ai-tool-finder/tool/chatgpt/
- Pricing: Free; Go $8/mo; Plus $20/mo; Pro $100–500/mo tiers (tier: freemium, free tier: yes)
- Best for: All-purpose chat, research, and OpenAI stack users
- Skill levels: beginner, intermediate, advanced
- Strengths: Broadest general assistant; Deep Research and Agent modes; Huge ecosystem (Codex, GPTs, apps)
- Weaknesses: Plan ladder can get expensive; Writing style sometimes generic vs Claude

### Claude
- Website: https://claude.ai
- Page: https://itscloudy96.github.io/ai-tool-finder/tool/claude/
- Pricing: Free; Pro $20/mo ($17 annual); Max $100–200/mo (tier: freemium, free tier: yes)
- Best for: Writing, coding, and thoughtful long-form work
- Skill levels: beginner, intermediate, advanced
- Strengths: Excellent writing and coding; Artifacts + Claude Code; Strong long-context reasoning
- Weaknesses: Usage limits on Pro for heavy users; Fewer consumer integrations than ChatGPT/Gemini

### Google Gemini
- Website: https://gemini.google.com
- Page: https://itscloudy96.github.io/ai-tool-finder/tool/gemini/
- Pricing: Free; Google AI Plus $4.99/mo; AI Pro $19.99/mo; Ultra $99.99–$199.99/mo (tier: freemium, free tier: yes)
- Best for: Google Workspace users needing chat + image/video in one place
- Skill levels: beginner, intermediate, advanced
- Strengths: Deep Google Workspace integration; Strong multimodal (images + Veo video); Good value entry paid tier
- Weaknesses: Best when you live in Google apps; Feature naming churn

### Grok
- Website: https://grok.com
- Page: https://itscloudy96.github.io/ai-tool-finder/tool/grok/
- Pricing: Free limited; X Plus $8/mo; Premium $30/mo; Super $100/mo; Ultra $200/mo (tier: freemium, free tier: yes)
- Best for: Real-time social/tech pulse and X-native creators
- Skill levels: beginner, intermediate, advanced
- Strengths: Real-time X firehose context; Grok Imagine for images/video; Competitive API pricing / large context
- Weaknesses: Tied to X subscription ladder; Grok Bot not on Plus

### DeepSeek
- Website: https://www.deepseek.com
- Page: https://itscloudy96.github.io/ai-tool-finder/tool/deepseek/
- Pricing: App/web chat commonly free; API pay-per-token (tier: freemium, free tier: yes)
- Best for: Budget coding/reasoning and open-model experimentation
- Skill levels: beginner, intermediate, advanced
- Strengths: Strong open-model reasoning; Toggleable deep thinking; Cheap API for builders
- Weaknesses: Consumer UX less polished than ChatGPT/Claude; Trust/compliance concerns for some orgs

### LangGraph
- Website: https://www.langchain.com/langgraph
- Page: https://itscloudy96.github.io/ai-tool-finder/tool/langgraph/
- Pricing: Open-source (MIT); LangSmith observability paid for teams (tier: freemium, free tier: yes)
- Best for: Complex durable multi-agent workflows in Python/JS
- Skill levels: advanced
- Strengths: Stateful graph orchestration; Checkpoints and human-in-the-loop; Provider-flexible
- Weaknesses: Steeper learning curve; Overkill for simple agents

### CrewAI
- Website: https://www.crewai.com
- Page: https://itscloudy96.github.io/ai-tool-finder/tool/crewai/
- Pricing: Open-source core; cloud/enterprise extras paid (tier: freemium, free tier: yes)
- Best for: Quick role-based multi-agent prototypes
- Skill levels: intermediate, advanced
- Strengths: Intuitive role-based crews; Fast multi-agent prototypes; MCP support
- Weaknesses: Can burn tokens with many agents; Less explicit graphs than LangGraph

### OpenAI Agents SDK
- Website: https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-python/
- Page: https://itscloudy96.github.io/ai-tool-finder/tool/openai-agents-sdk/
- Pricing: Open-source SDK (MIT); pay OpenAI API usage (tier: freemium, free tier: yes)
- Best for: OpenAI-first apps needing small composable agent primitives
- Skill levels: intermediate, advanced
- Strengths: Lightweight handoffs and guardrails; Clean primitives; OpenAI-first
- Weaknesses: Best with OpenAI models; Tracing may send data to OpenAI

### Claude Agent SDK
- Website: https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/agents-and-tools/claude-agent-sdk/overview
- Page: https://itscloudy96.github.io/ai-tool-finder/tool/claude-agent-sdk/
- Pricing: SDK available; usage via Claude API / Anthropic commercial terms (tier: paid, free tier: no)
- Best for: Coding, research, and computer-use agents around Claude
- Skill levels: advanced
- Strengths: Built-in file/shell/MCP tools; Permissions, hooks, subagents; Strong coding/computer-use agents
- Weaknesses: Claude-oriented; Commercial terms apply

### Google ADK
- Website: https://google.github.io/adk-docs/
- Page: https://itscloudy96.github.io/ai-tool-finder/tool/google-adk/
- Pricing: Open-source (Apache 2.0); pay for Gemini/GCP runtime (tier: freemium, free tier: yes)
- Best for: GCP-native multimodal agent systems
- Skill levels: advanced
- Strengths: Multi-language (Python/TS/Go/Java); Workflow + graph agents; GCP/Gemini native
- Weaknesses: Best fit is Google Cloud; Younger ecosystem than LangChain

### Mastra
- Website: https://mastra.ai
- Page: https://itscloudy96.github.io/ai-tool-finder/tool/mastra/
- Pricing: Open-source TypeScript framework (tier: free, free tier: yes)
- Best for: TypeScript teams building production agents
- Skill levels: intermediate, advanced
- Strengths: TS-native agents + workflows; Memory and Studio; Suspend-and-resume patterns
- Weaknesses: TypeScript-focused; Smaller community than LangChain

### Pydantic AI
- Website: https://ai.pydantic.dev
- Page: https://itscloudy96.github.io/ai-tool-finder/tool/pydantic-ai/
- Pricing: Open-source; pay for models/durable engines you attach (tier: free, free tier: yes)
- Best for: Python teams who want typed, testable agents
- Skill levels: advanced
- Strengths: Type-safe Python agents; Structured outputs; Durable execution integrations
- Weaknesses: Requires Python expertise; Orchestration extras are DIY

### LlamaIndex Workflows
- Website: https://www.llamaindex.ai
- Page: https://itscloudy96.github.io/ai-tool-finder/tool/llamaindex/
- Pricing: Open-source; cloud extras paid (tier: freemium, free tier: yes)
- Best for: Document-heavy retrieval agents and data pipelines
- Skill levels: intermediate, advanced
- Strengths: Event-driven doc/data pipelines; Strong RAG heritage; Typed events/steps
- Weaknesses: Heavier for simple chatbots; Learning curve for workflows

### Godot MCP Studio
- Website: https://www.godotmcpstudio.com
- Page: https://itscloudy96.github.io/ai-tool-finder/tool/godot-mcp-studio/
- Pricing: Lite free; Pro ~€39 one-time (+ image credits) (tier: freemium, free tier: yes)
- Best for: Indie/jam developers vibe-coding Godot games with agents
- Skill levels: intermediate, advanced
- Strengths: Lets Claude Code/Cursor drive Godot live; Playtest tools on Pro; Pairs with text-friendly Godot projects
- Weaknesses: Godot-specific; Still need a coding agent subscription

### Unity AI (MCP + Assistant)
- Website: https://unity.com/ai
- Page: https://itscloudy96.github.io/ai-tool-finder/tool/unity-ai/
- Pricing: CLI/MCP/plugin free; in-editor assistant credits (included on Pro+; Personal trial then ~$10/mo) (tier: freemium, free tier: yes)
- Best for: Unity developers connecting coding agents into the editor
- Skill levels: intermediate, advanced
- Strengths: Official MCP server/CLI for Unity 6+; Works with Claude Code/Codex/Cursor; Editor + agent loop
- Weaknesses: Requires Unity 6+; Assistant credits can add cost on Personal

### Phaser + AI coding assistant
- Website: https://phaser.io
- Page: https://itscloudy96.github.io/ai-tool-finder/tool/phaser-cursor/
- Pricing: Phaser open-source free; pair with Cursor/Claude Code/Copilot subscriptions (tier: freemium, free tier: yes)
- Best for: Vibe-coded browser games with Cursor/Claude Code
- Skill levels: beginner, intermediate
- Strengths: Browser games as shareable links; Dense training data for agents; Simple deploy path
- Weaknesses: Not a single product (stack); You assemble tooling

## Vibe coding & app builders
Vibe coding tools and AI app builders that turn a prompt into a working app or website.

### Cursor
- Website: https://cursor.com
- Page: https://itscloudy96.github.io/ai-tool-finder/tool/cursor/
- Pricing: Free (limited); Plus from ~$8/mo (Grok-only); Pro ~$16–30/mo; usage meters apply (tier: freemium, free tier: yes)
- Best for: Complex multi-file projects and daily vibe coding in a dedicated AI IDE
- Skill levels: beginner, intermediate, advanced
- Strengths: AI-native VS Code fork; Strong multi-file agent/Composer; Codebase indexing and MCP
- Weaknesses: Must switch editors; Usage meters can surprise heavy users; Steeper for non-developers

### Claude Code
- Website: https://claude.ai/code

- Best for: Large codebases, terminal agents, and long-horizon debugging
- Skill levels: intermediate, advanced
- Strengths: 1M-token context for large repos; Terminal-first autonomous refactors; Strong planning and git workflows
- Weaknesses: Free tier too limited for real coding; CLI learning curve; Shares Claude chat usage pool

- Best for: Beginners who want a playable browser game today

## AI agents & automation
Frameworks, SDKs and no-code platforms for building AI agents and automating workflows.

- Website: https://ai.pydantic.dev
- Page: https://itscloudy96.github.io/ai-tool-finder/tool/pydantic-ai/
- Pricing: Open-source; pay for models/durable engines you attach (tier: free, free tier: yes)
- Best for: Python teams who want typed, testable agents
- Skill levels: advanced
- Strengths: Type-safe Python agents; Structured outputs; Durable execution integrations
- Weaknesses: Requires Python expertise; Orchestration extras are DIY

### LlamaIndex Workflows
- Website: https://www.llamaindex.ai
- Page: https://itscloudy96.github.io/ai-tool-finder/tool/llamaindex/
- Pricing: Open-source; cloud extras paid (tier: freemium, free tier: yes)
- Best for: Document-heavy retrieval agents and data pipelines
- Skill levels: intermediate, advanced
- Strengths: Event-driven doc/data pipelines; Strong RAG heritage; Typed events/steps
- Weaknesses: Heavier for simple chatbots; Learning curve for workflows

### n8n AI Agents
- Website: https://n8n.io
- Page: https://itscloudy96.github.io/ai-tool-finder/tool/n8n/
- Pricing: Free self-host; cloud plans paid (tier: freemium, free tier: yes)
- Best for: No/low-code agent automations across SaaS apps
- Skill levels: beginner, intermediate
- Strengths: Visual workflows + AI nodes; Self-hostable; Great for ops automations
- Weaknesses: Not a coding IDE; Complex agents need careful design

### Dify
- Website: https://dify.ai
- Page: https://itscloudy96.github.io/ai-tool-finder/tool/dify/
- Pricing: Open-source self-host; cloud plans paid (tier: freemium, free tier: yes)
- Best for: Teams building internal AI apps without heavy engineering
- Skill levels: beginner, intermediate
- Strengths: Visual LLM app builder; RAG and agents in one UI; Good for internal tools
- Weaknesses: Less flexible than code SDKs for complex agents; Hosting ops if self-hosted

### Godot MCP Studio
- Website: https://www.godotmcpstudio.com
- Page: https://itscloudy96.github.io/ai-tool-finder/tool/godot-mcp-studio/
- Pricing: Lite free; Pro ~€39 one-time (+ image credits) (tier: freemium, free tier: yes)
- Best for: Indie/jam developers vibe-coding Godot games with agents
- Skill levels: intermediate, advanced
- Strengths: Lets Claude Code/Cursor drive Godot live; Playtest tools on Pro; Pairs with text-friendly Godot projects
- Weaknesses: Godot-specific; Still need a coding agent subscription

### Unity AI (MCP + Assistant)
- Website: https://unity.com/ai
- Page: https://itscloudy96.github.io/ai-tool-finder/tool/unity-ai/
- Pricing: CLI/MCP/plugin free; in-editor assistant credits (included on Pro+; Personal trial then ~$10/mo) (tier: freemium, free tier: yes)
- Best for: Unity developers connecting coding agents into the editor
- Skill levels: intermediate, advanced
- Strengths: Official MCP server/CLI for Unity 6+; Works with Claude Code/Codex/Cursor; Editor + agent loop
- Weaknesses: Requires Unity 6+; Assistant credits can add cost on Personal

### Zapier (AI by Zapier)
- Website: https://zapier.com
- Page: https://itscloudy96.github.io/ai-tool-finder/tool/zapier/
- Pricing: Free (100 tasks/mo, AI steps preview only); Professional from $19.99/mo annual ($29.99 monthly) (tier: freemium, free tier: yes)
- Best for: No-code automations and simple AI agents across your apps
- Skill levels: beginner, intermediate
- Strengths: Connects 7,000+ apps; AI steps and agents inside workflows; No code required
- Weaknesses: AI workflows need a paid plan; Task-based pricing adds up

## Game development
AI tools for game development: prototyping, assets, engines, 3D models, music and voice.

### Replit Agent

- Best for: Beginners and fast browser-hosted prototypes
- Skill levels: beginner, intermediate
- Strengths: Browser IDE, no local setup; Agent asks clarifying questions first; Build and host in one place
- Weaknesses: Less stack control than local IDEs; Agent occasionally over-claims fixes

### Udio

- Best for: Sketching song ideas and soundtrack concepts fast
- Skill levels: beginner, intermediate
- Strengths: Full songs with vocals from a text prompt; Lyric editor and song extensions; Cheap credit packs that never expire
- Weaknesses: Audio/stem downloads currently disabled on all plans; Subscription credits do not roll over

### Meshy
- Website: https://www.meshy.ai
- Page: https://itscloudy96.github.io/ai-tool-finder/tool/meshy/
- Pricing: Free (100 credits/mo, attribution); Pro $20/mo (1,000 credits) (tier: freemium, free tier: yes)
- Best for: Quick 3D props and prototype assets for indie games
- Skill levels: beginner, intermediate
- Strengths: Text/image to 3D models; Game-ready exports and API on Pro; Commercial use available
- Weaknesses: Free tier has low queue priority and limited downloads; Models often need cleanup for production

## Image generation
AI image generators for art, concept design, logos, game assets and marketing visuals.

### ChatGPT
- Website: https://chatgpt.com
- Page: https://itscloudy96.github.io/ai-tool-finder/tool/chatgpt/
- Pricing: Free; Go $8/mo; Plus $20/mo; Pro $100–500/mo tiers (tier: freemium, free tier: yes)
- Best for: All-purpose chat, research, and OpenAI stack users
- Skill levels: beginner, intermediate, advanced
- Strengths: Broadest general assistant; Deep Research and Agent modes; Huge ecosystem (Codex, GPTs, apps)
- Weaknesses: Plan ladder can get expensive; Writing style sometimes generic vs Claude

### Google Gemini
- Website: https://gemini.google.com
- Page: https://itscloudy96.github.io/ai-tool-finder/tool/gemini/
- Pricing: Free; Google AI Plus $4.99/mo; AI Pro $19.99/mo; Ultra $99.99–$199.99/mo (tier: freemium, free tier: yes)
- Best for: Google Workspace users needing chat + image/video in one place
- Skill levels: beginner, intermediate, advanced
- Strengths: Deep Google Workspace integration; Strong multimodal (images + Veo video); Good value entry paid tier
- Weaknesses: Best when you live in Google apps; Feature naming churn

### Grok
- Website: https://grok.com
- Page: https://itscloudy96.github.io/ai-tool-finder/tool/grok/
- Pricing: Free limited; X Plus $8/mo; Premium $30/mo; Super $100/mo; Ultra $200/mo (tier: freemium, free tier: yes)
- Best for: Real-time social/tech pulse and X-native creators
- Skill levels: beginner, intermediate, advanced
- Strengths: Real-time X firehose context; Grok Imagine for images/video; Competitive API pricing / large context
- Weaknesses: Tied to X subscription ladder; Grok Bot not on Plus

### Poe
- Website: https://poe.com
- Page: https://itscloudy96.github.io/ai-tool-finder/tool/poe/
- Pricing: Free; paid from ~$4.99–$19.99/mo depending on plan (tier: freemium, free tier: yes)
- Best for: Trying multiple AI models without many subscriptions
- Skill levels: beginner, intermediate
- Strengths: Many models in one place; Side-by-side comparisons; Points-based compute
- Weaknesses: Not specialized for coding agents; Quality depends on which model you pick

### Meta AI
- Website: https://www.meta.ai
- Page: https://itscloudy96.github.io/ai-tool-finder/tool/meta-ai/
- Pricing: Free (tier: free, free tier: yes)
- Best for: Casual free chat and social creative generation
- Skill levels: beginner
- Strengths: Free chat + image + short video vibes; Lives in Meta apps; Low barrier
- Weaknesses: Less powerful for serious coding/research; Privacy tied to Meta ecosystem

### Midjourney
- Website: https://www.midjourney.com
- Page: https://itscloudy96.github.io/ai-tool-finder/tool/midjourney/
- Pricing: No free tier; Basic from ~$10/mo (tier: paid, free tier: no)
- Best for: Artistic concept art, stylized visuals, and moodboards
- Skill levels: beginner, intermediate, advanced
- Strengths: Top artistic/cinematic stills (V8); Strong style control; Midjourney Video for animating stills
- Weaknesses: No classic public API; Weak text-in-image vs Ideogram; Paid-only

### FLUX (Black Forest Labs)
- Website: https://bfl.ai
- Page: https://itscloudy96.github.io/ai-tool-finder/tool/flux/
- Pricing: API ~$0.01+/image via partners; open weights for self-host; also via Krea/Freepik (tier: freemium, free tier: yes)
- Best for: Product photos, pipelines, and developer image APIs
- Skill levels: intermediate, advanced
- Strengths: Photorealism leader; API-first / LoRA fine-tuning; Open-weight options
- Weaknesses: No polished first-party consumer app; Quality depends on host

### Ideogram
- Website: https://ideogram.ai
- Page: https://itscloudy96.github.io/ai-tool-finder/tool/ideogram/
- Pricing: Free (~10 images/day); paid from ~$7/mo (tier: freemium, free tier: yes)
- Best for: Thumbnails, posters, and any image that must include readable text
- Skill levels: beginner, intermediate
- Strengths: Best-in-class text in images; Posters, logos, thumbnails; Affordable
- Weaknesses: Less artistic than Midjourney; Not a video tool

### Adobe Firefly
- Website: https://www.adobe.com/products/firefly.html
- Page: https://itscloudy96.github.io/ai-tool-finder/tool/adobe-firefly/
- Pricing: Free limited credits; Standard from ~$9.99/mo; also via Creative Cloud (tier: freemium, free tier: yes)
- Best for: Professionals needing commercially safe generative fill in Adobe apps
- Skill levels: beginner, intermediate
- Strengths: Commercial IP indemnification; Photoshop/Illustrator integration; Brand-safe training data story
- Weaknesses: Less cutting-edge aesthetics than Midjourney/FLUX for some styles

### Leonardo.AI
- Website: https://leonardo.ai
- Page: https://itscloudy96.github.io/ai-tool-finder/tool/leonardo/
- Pricing: Free daily tokens; paid from ~$10–12/mo (tier: freemium, free tier: yes)
- Best for: Game art, characters, and consistent asset packs
- Skill levels: beginner, intermediate
- Strengths: Game assets and concept art; Character consistency; Custom model training
- Weaknesses: Token economy to learn; Video secondary vs dedicated video tools

### Stable Diffusion
- Website: https://stability.ai
- Page: https://itscloudy96.github.io/ai-tool-finder/tool/stable-diffusion/
- Pricing: Free self-hosted; commercial licenses/cloud hosts vary (tier: free, free tier: yes)
- Best for: Privacy-first local image generation and custom models
- Skill levels: intermediate, advanced
- Strengths: Fully local/private; Huge LoRA/community model ecosystem; Unlimited when self-hosted
- Weaknesses: Setup friction; Quality depends on model choice and GPU

### Recraft
- Website: https://www.recraft.ai
- Page: https://itscloudy96.github.io/ai-tool-finder/tool/recraft/
- Pricing: Free with limits; Pro from ~$12–25/mo (tier: freemium, free tier: yes)
- Best for: Logos, icons, and vector brand assets
- Skill levels: beginner, intermediate
- Strengths: True SVG/vector output; Logos and icons; Brand design focus
- Weaknesses: Not for photoreal scenes; Paid for heavy use

### ChatGPT Images (GPT Image)
- Website: https://chatgpt.com
- Page: https://itscloudy96.github.io/ai-tool-finder/tool/chatgpt-images/
- Pricing: Included with ChatGPT plans; API priced per image (tier: freemium, free tier: yes)
- Best for: Quick image generation/editing without leaving chat
- Skill levels: beginner, intermediate
- Strengths: Convenient inside ChatGPT; Strong editing/inpainting; Good text rendering for many use cases
- Weaknesses: Limits depend on ChatGPT plan; Less style control than Midjourney

### Meshy
- Website: https://www.meshy.ai
- Page: https://itscloudy96.github.io/ai-tool-finder/tool/meshy/

### Otter.ai
- Website: https://otter.ai
- Page: https://itscloudy96.github.io/ai-tool-finder/tool/otter/
- Pricing: Basic free (300 min/mo); Pro $16.99/mo ($8.33/mo annual); Business $30/user/mo ($19.99 annual) (tier: freemium, free tier: yes)
- Best for: Meeting transcripts and searchable notes
- Skill levels: beginner, intermediate
- Strengths: Live meeting transcription for Zoom, Meet, Teams; AI chat across meetings; Has an MCP server
- Weaknesses: Free plan caps conversations at 30 min; Meeting bot joins your calls

## Writing & chat assistants
AI chat assistants and writing tools for drafting, brainstorming and everyday questions.

### ChatGPT
- Website: https://chatgpt.com
- Page: https://itscloudy96.github.io/ai-tool-finder/tool/chatgpt/
- Pricing: Free; Go $8/mo; Plus $20/mo; Pro $100–500/mo tiers (tier: freemium, free tier: yes)
- Best for: All-purpose chat, research, and OpenAI stack users
- Skill levels: beginner, intermediate, advanced
- Strengths: Broadest general assistant; Deep Research and Agent modes; Huge ecosystem (Codex, GPTs, apps)
- Weaknesses: Plan ladder can get expensive; Writing style sometimes generic vs Claude

### Claude
- Website: https://claude.ai
- Page: https://itscloudy96.github.io/ai-tool-finder/tool/claude/
- Pricing: Free; Pro $20/mo ($17 annual); Max $100–200/mo (tier: freemium, free tier: yes)
- Best for: Writing, coding, and thoughtful long-form work
- Skill levels: beginner, intermediate, advanced
- Strengths: Excellent writing and coding; Artifacts + Claude Code; Strong long-context reasoning
- Weaknesses: Usage limits on Pro for heavy users; Fewer consumer integrations than ChatGPT/Gemini

### Google Gemini
- Website: https://gemini.google.com
- Page: https://itscloudy96.github.io/ai-tool-finder/tool/gemini/
- Pricing: Free; Google AI Plus $4.99/mo; AI Pro $19.99/mo; Ultra $99.99–$199.99/mo (tier: freemium, free tier: yes)
- Best for: Google Workspace users needing chat + image/video in one place
- Skill levels: beginner, intermediate, advanced
- Strengths: Deep Google Workspace integration; Strong multimodal (images + Veo video); Good value entry paid tier
- Weaknesses: Best when you live in Google apps; Feature naming churn

### Grok
- Website: https://grok.com
- Page: https://itscloudy96.github.io/ai-tool-finder/tool/grok/
- Pricing: Free limited; X Plus $8/mo; Premium $30/mo; Super $100/mo; Ultra $200/mo (tier: freemium, free tier: yes)
- Best for: Real-time social/tech pulse and X-native creators
- Skill levels: beginner, intermediate, advanced
- Strengths: Real-time X firehose context; Grok Imagine for images/video; Competitive API pricing / large context
- Weaknesses: Tied to X subscription ladder; Grok Bot not on Plus

### Perplexity
- Website: https://www.perplexity.ai
- Page: https://itscloudy96.github.io/ai-tool-finder/tool/perplexity/
- Pricing: Free; Pro ~$17/mo annual (~$20 monthly); Max ~$167/mo annual (tier: freemium, free tier: yes)
- Best for: Sourced research and internet deep dives
- Skill levels: beginner, intermediate, advanced
- Strengths: Citations by default; Search/Research/Labs modes; Premium data sources on Pro
- Weaknesses: Not a full coding IDE; Advanced Computer features need Pro/Max

### Microsoft Copilot
- Website: https://copilot.microsoft.com
- Page: https://itscloudy96.github.io/ai-tool-finder/tool/microsoft-copilot/
- Pricing: Free Copilot app; Microsoft 365 Personal $9.99/mo; Premium $19.99/mo (tier: freemium, free tier: yes)
- Best for: Office workers living in Word, Excel, Outlook, Teams
- Skill levels: beginner, intermediate
- Strengths: Microsoft 365 integration; Copilot Vision; Office-native drafting
- Weaknesses: Deepest value locked in M365; Less developer-agent depth than Cursor/Claude

### DeepSeek
- Website: https://www.deepseek.com
- Page: https://itscloudy96.github.io/ai-tool-finder/tool/deepseek/
- Pricing: App/web chat commonly free; API pay-per-token (tier: freemium, free tier: yes)
- Best for: Budget coding/reasoning and open-model experimentation
- Skill levels: beginner, intermediate, advanced
- Strengths: Strong open-model reasoning; Toggleable deep thinking; Cheap API for builders
- Weaknesses: Consumer UX less polished than ChatGPT/Claude; Trust/compliance concerns for some orgs

### Poe
- Website: https://poe.com
- Page: https://itscloudy96.github.io/ai-tool-finder/tool/poe/
- Pricing: Free; paid from ~$4.99–$19.99/mo depending on plan (tier: freemium, free tier: yes)
- Best for: Trying multiple AI models without many subscriptions
- Skill levels: beginner, intermediate
- Strengths: Many models in one place; Side-by-side comparisons; Points-based compute
- Weaknesses: Not specialized for coding agents; Quality depends on which model you pick

### Meta AI
- Website: https://www.meta.ai
- Page: https://itscloudy96.github.io/ai-tool-finder/tool/meta-ai/
- Pricing: Free (tier: free, free tier: yes)
- Best for: Casual free chat and social creative generation
- Skill levels: beginner
- Strengths: Free chat + image + short video vibes; Lives in Meta apps; Low barrier
- Weaknesses: Less powerful for serious coding/research; Privacy tied to Meta ecosystem

### Notion AI
- Website: https://www.notion.com/product/ai
- Page: https://itscloudy96.github.io/ai-tool-finder/tool/notion-ai/
- Pricing: Included with Notion paid plans (varies by workspace plan) (tier: paid, free tier: no)
- Best for: Teams already organizing work in Notion
- Skill levels: beginner, intermediate
- Strengths: Writes inside your docs/wiki; Good for notes to drafts; Team knowledge context
- Weaknesses: Requires Notion subscription; Weaker than Claude/ChatGPT for hard reasoning

### Dify
- Website: https://dify.ai
- Page: https://itscloudy96.github.io/ai-tool-finder/tool/dify/
- Pricing: Open-source self-host; cloud plans paid (tier: freemium, free tier: yes)
- Best for: Teams building internal AI apps without heavy engineering
- Skill levels: beginner, intermediate
- Strengths: Visual LLM app builder; RAG and agents in one UI; Good for internal tools
- Weaknesses: Less flexible than code SDKs for complex agents; Hosting ops if self-hosted

### Gamma
- Website: https://gamma.app
- Page: https://itscloudy96.github.io/ai-tool-finder/tool/gamma/
- Pricing: Free (400 one-time credits); Plus $9/mo annual ($12 monthly); Pro $18/mo annual ($25 monthly) (tier: freemium, free tier: yes)
- Best for: Pitch decks, game design docs and quick landing pages
- Skill levels: beginner, intermediate
- Strengths: Decks, docs and one-page sites from a prompt; Exports to PPTX and Google Slides; Custom domains on Pro
- Weaknesses: Free credits do not refill; Generated decks still need editing

### NotebookLM (Gemini Notebook)
- Website: https://notebooklm.google.com
- Page: https://itscloudy96.github.io/ai-tool-finder/tool/notebooklm/
- Pricing: Free with a Google account; higher limits with Google AI Pro ($19.99/mo) (tier: freemium, free tier: yes)
- Best for: Studying docs, papers and patch notes with citations
- Skill levels: beginner, intermediate, advanced
- Strengths: Grounded answers from your own sources; Audio overviews (podcast-style summaries); Generous free limits
- Weaknesses: Works only over sources you add; Google account required

## Productivity & meetings
AI productivity tools for meetings, notes, slides and automating busywork.

### Microsoft Copilot

- Page: https://itscloudy96.github.io/ai-tool-finder/tool/microsoft-copilot/
- Pricing: Free Copilot app; Microsoft 365 Personal $9.99/mo; Premium $19.99/mo (tier: freemium, free tier: yes)

- Page: https://itscloudy96.github.io/ai-tool-finder/tool/n8n/
- Pricing: Free self-host; cloud plans paid (tier: freemium, free tier: yes)
- Best for: No/low-code agent automations across SaaS apps
- Skill levels: beginner, intermediate
- Strengths: Visual workflows + AI nodes; Self-hostable; Great for ops automations
- Weaknesses: Not a coding IDE; Complex agents need careful design

### Descript
- Website: https://www.descript.com
- Page: https://itscloudy96.github.io/ai-tool-finder/tool/descript/
- Pricing: Free (1 media hr/mo, watermark); Hobbyist $16/mo annual ($24 monthly); Creator $24/mo annual ($35 monthly) (tier: freemium, free tier: yes)
- Best for: Podcasts, YouTube edits and devlog videos
- Skill levels: beginner, intermediate
- Strengths: Edit video by editing the transcript; Studio Sound and filler-word removal; Underlord AI co-editor
- Weaknesses: Free exports are 720p with a watermark; Hobbyist plan cannot buy top-ups

### Otter.ai
- Website: https://otter.ai
- Page: https://itscloudy96.github.io/ai-tool-finder/tool/otter/
- Pricing: Basic free (300 min/mo); Pro $16.99/mo ($8.33/mo annual); Business $30/user/mo ($19.99 annual) (tier: freemium, free tier: yes)
- Best for: Meeting transcripts and searchable notes
- Skill levels: beginner, intermediate
- Strengths: Live meeting transcription for Zoom, Meet, Teams; AI chat across meetings; Has an MCP server
- Weaknesses: Free plan caps conversations at 30 min; Meeting bot joins your calls

### Granola
- Website: https://www.granola.ai
- Page: https://itscloudy96.github.io/ai-tool-finder/tool/granola/
- Pricing: Basic free (30-day history); Business $14/user/mo; Enterprise $35/user/mo (tier: freemium, free tier: yes)
- Best for: Clean AI meeting notes without a bot in the call
- Skill levels: beginner, intermediate
- Strengths: Bot-free meeting notes from device audio; Templates and AI chat across meetings; MCP integration for Claude/ChatGPT
- Weaknesses: Free plan only shows last 30 days; Integrations need Business

### Zapier (AI by Zapier)
- Website: https://zapier.com
- Page: https://itscloudy96.github.io/ai-tool-finder/tool/zapier/
- Pricing: Free (100 tasks/mo, AI steps preview only); Professional from $19.99/mo annual ($29.99 monthly) (tier: freemium, free tier: yes)
- Best for: No-code automations and simple AI agents across your apps
- Skill levels: beginner, intermediate
- Strengths: Connects 7,000+ apps; AI steps and agents inside workflows; No code required
- Weaknesses: AI workflows need a paid plan; Task-based pricing adds up
